facts.statement: Razanandrongobe was a carnivorous ziphosuchian crocodyliform that lived in Madagascar during the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Razanandrongobe (meaning "ancestor [of the] large lizard" in Malagasy) is a genus of carnivorous ziphosuchian crocodyliform from the Middle Jurassic of Madagascar.

facts.statement: The only known species is Razanandrongobe sakalavae, named in 2004 by Simone Maganuco and colleagues.
facts.quote: It contains the type and only species Razanandrongobe sakalavae, named in 2004 by Simone Maganuco and colleagues based on isolated bones found in 2003.

facts.statement: The initial fossils, including a maxilla fragment and teeth, were found in the Bathonian-aged Sakaraha Formation near Mahajanga, Madagascar.
facts.quote: The remains, which included a fragment of maxilla and teeth, originated from the Bathonian-aged Sakaraha Formation of Mahajanga, Madagascar.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe had adaptations for eating bones and tendons, including large serrated teeth and reinforced bony structures in its palate and teeth.
facts.quote: Razanandrongobe shows a number of adaptations to a diet containing bones and tendons, including teeth with large serrations and bony structures reinforcing its palate and teeth.

facts.statement: At 7 meters long, Razanandrongobe was the largest known member of the Notosuchia and likely occupied a predatory niche similar to theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Measuring 7 m long, it was the largest member of the Notosuchia and may have occupied a predatory ecological niche similar to theropods.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe is the oldest known member of the Notosuchia, filling a 74-million-year gap in the group's evolutionary history.
facts.quote: These remains allowed them to confidently assign Razanandrongobe as the oldest-known member of the Notosuchia, a group of crocodylomorphs, which partially filled a gap of 74 million years in the group's evolutionary history.

facts.statement: A privately funded expedition by teams from the Milan Natural History Museum and the Civic Museum of Fossils of Besano was launched in April 2003.
facts.quote: In April 2003, a joint team from the Milan Natural History Museum (MSNM) and Civic Museum of Fossils of Besano launched a privately funded expedition to the region.

facts.statement: Simone Maganuco, Cristiano Dal Sasso, and Giovanni Pasini described the holotype specimen MSNM V5770 as the new genus and species Razanandrongobe sakalavae in 2006.
facts.quote: Simone Maganuco, Cristiano Dal Sasso, and Pasini described these specimens in 2006 as representing a new genus and species, Razanandrongobe sakalavae, with MSNM V5770 as the holotype.

facts.statement: The genus name Razanandrongobe is derived from Malagasy words meaning "ancestor of the large lizard".
facts.quote: The genus name is a composite of the Malagasy words "razana-" (ancestor), "androngo-" (lizard), and "-be" (large), collectively meaning "ancestor of the large lizard".

facts.statement: Additional specimens, including skull fragments and a tooth crown, were described in 2017 by Dal Sasso, Pasini, Maganuco, and Guillaume Fleury.
facts.quote: All of these additional specimens were described in 2017 by Dal Sasso, Pasini, Maganuco, and Guillaume Fleury.

facts.statement: Researchers inferred that Razanandrongobe had a body shape similar to Baurusuchidae, measuring 7 meters long, 1.6 meters high at the hip, and weighing 800 to 1000 kilograms.
facts.quote: Dal Sasso and colleagues inferred a body shape similar to the Baurusuchidae, producing an overall length of 7 m, a height at the hip of 1.6 m, and a weight of 800 - 1000 kg.

facts.statement: Uniquely, the tip of Razanandrongobe's lower jaw was toothless, spanning the diameter of more than one tooth.
facts.quote: Uniquely, the tip of the lower jaw was devoid of teeth, for a section of the dentary corresponding to the diameter of more than one tooth.

facts.statement: The tip of Razanandrongobe's lower jaw was upturned at an angle of about 50 degrees to strengthen it.
facts.quote: The tip of the lower jaw would have been strengthened by being upturned at an angle of about 50°.

facts.statement: The teeth of Razanandrongobe bore large serrations on both front and rear edges that were proportionally larger than those of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The teeth themselves are unusual; they bear large serrations on both the front and rear edges, which are proportionally even larger than those of dinosaurs such as Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The teeth of Razanandrongobe were thick, non-constricted, and slightly recurved, a condition known as pachydont.
facts.quote: They were also thick, non-constricted, and slightly recurved (pachydont).

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe was heterodont, featuring U-shaped front teeth, incisiform side teeth, and globe-shaped rear teeth.
facts.quote: Several types of teeth are present, making Razanandrongobe heterodont: the teeth at the front of the jaw were U-shaped (or salinon-shaped) in cross-section, while those on the sides were incisiform (incisor-like) and sub-oval in cross-section, with the smallest teeth at the rear being globe-shaped.

facts.statement: In 2017, Dal Sasso and colleagues refined the phylogenetic placement of Razanandrongobe following the discovery of additional specimens.
facts.quote: Subsequently, the discovery of additional specimens allowed Dal Sasso and colleagues to refine the phylogenetic placement of Razanandrongobe in 2017.

facts.statement: In 2024, Razanandrongobe was recovered as a non-baurusuchid baurusuchian.
facts.quote: In 2024, Razanandrongobe was recovered as a non-baurusuchid baurusuchian.

facts.statement: Maganuco and colleagues debated whether unfused interdental plates were a synapomorphy of Archosauriformes or a plesiomorphic characteristic of crocodyliforms, theropods, and poposaurids.
facts.quote: Maganuco and colleagues suggested that unfused interdental plates are either a synapomorphy of Archosauriformes, or a plesiomorphic (ancestrally present) characteristic of crocodyliforms, theropods, and poposaurids.

facts.statement: The original material of Razanandrongobe was considered too fragmentary for phylogenetic analysis of archosauriforms because it lacked nearly all characteristics used in such analyses.
facts.quote: However, the original material of Razanandrongobe, consisting of a maxilla and teeth, was too fragmentary to be included in a phylogenetic analysis of archosauriforms, since it lacks nearly all characteristics used in such analyses.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe lived 42 million years before the oldest known notosuchians.
facts.quote: Razanandrongobe predates all of these notosuchians by 42 million years

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe fossils date to the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic, between 167.7 and 164.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: the Sakaraha Formation has been correlated to the Bathonian stage (167.7–164.7 million years ago) of the Middle Jurassic epoch

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe is classified within the family Sebecosuchia.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Sebecosuchia

facts.statement: The genus Razanandrongobe was named by Maganuco and colleagues in 2006.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Maganuco et al., 2006

facts.statement: Researchers initially hesitated to assign Razanandrongobe to a specific group because its fragmentary remains resembled both theropod dinosaurs and crocodilian lineages.
facts.quote: Aunque claramente estos pertenecían a un miembro de Archosauria, sus descubridores se rehusaron a asignar a este género a un grupo específico debido a que los restos fragmentarios se parecían a diferentes linajes de los dinosaurios terópodos y los crocodilomorfos

facts.statement: Additional remains including a premaxilla and jaws were discovered in 1972 but not described until 2017 by Cristiano Dal Sasso and colleagues.
facts.quote: Restos adicionales (incluyendo un premaxilar y mandíbulas) habían sido descubiertos ya en 1972, pero no fueron descritos hasta 2017 por Cristiano Dal Sasso y colaboradores

facts.statement: Giovanni Pasini first verified the presence of fossil-bearing strata in the region in October 2001.
facts.quote: En octubre de 2001, Giovanni Pasini verificó inicialmente la presencia de estratos fosilíferos en esta región

facts.statement: Simone Maganuco, Cristiano Dal Sasso, and Pasini described the specimens as the new genus and species Razanandrongobe sakalavae in 2006, with MSNM V5770 as the holotype.
facts.quote: Simone Maganuco, Cristiano Dal Sasso y Pasini describieron estos especímenes en 2006 como un nuevo género y especie, Razanandrongobe sakalavae, siendo MSNM V5770 su holotipo

facts.statement: The genus name Razanandrongobe combines Malagasy words meaning "ancestor of the great lizard".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se compone de las palabras malgaches "razana-" (ancestro), "androngo-" (lagarto) y "-be" (grande), significando unidas "ancestro del gran lagarto"

facts.statement: The species name sakalavae refers to the Sakalava ethnic group inhabiting the region.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie proviene del latín "de Sakalava", en referencia al grupo étnico que habita la región

facts.statement: All known Razanandrongobe fossils come from the Sakaraha Formation in the dry lands around Ambondromamy, Madagascar.
facts.quote: Todos los restos conocidos de Razanandrongobe se originan de estratos pertenecientes a la Formación Sakaraha en las tierras yermas (conocidas localmente como tanety) que rodean al pueblo de Ambondromamy, Madagascar

facts.statement: The holotype is a right maxilla fragment measuring 192 mm long, 124 mm high, and 96 mm wide.
facts.quote: Está basado en el holotipo MSNM V5770, un fragmento de maxilar derecho, el hueso que alberga la mayoría de los dientes en la mandíbula superior, el cual mide 192 milímetros de largo, 124 mm de alto y 96 mm de ancho

facts.statement: At 7 meters in length, Razanandrongobe is the largest known member of Notosuchia.
facts.quote: Con 7 metros de longitud, es el mayor miembro de Notosuchia

facts.statement: Wear patterns on Razanandrongobe's teeth suggest it bit into bones or other hard objects.
facts.quote: They inferred that these wear surfaces more strongly resemble those resulting from tooth-food contact than from tooth-tooth contact, with the enamel having flaked off as the animal bit into bones or other hard objects

facts.statement: The environment where Razanandrongobe lived is inferred to have been river-based or lake-based.
facts.quote: The depositional environment has been inferred to be fluvial (river-based) or lacustrine (lake-based)

facts.statement: The close relationship between Razanandrongobe and the younger lineage Sebecosuchia is considered provisional by researchers.
facts.quote: however, for this reason, Dal Sasso and colleagues noted that its close relation to Sebecosuchia — a much younger lineage, being known from the Santonian forward — must be treated as provisional

facts.statement: The Museo di Storia Naturale di Milano acquired an additional specimen, a tooth crown cataloged as MSNM V7144.
facts.quote: El MSNM consiguió un espécimen adicional, una corona dental catalogada como MSNM V7144.

facts.statement: Additional Razanandrongobe specimens were described in 2017 by Dal Sasso, Pasini, Maganuco, and Guillaume Fleury.
facts.quote: Todos estos especímenes adicionales fueron descritos en 2017 por Dal Sasso, Pasini, Maganuco y Guillaume Fleury.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe is considered the largest known terrestrial Mesoeucrocodylia from the Jurassic and the largest Notosuchian overall.
facts.quote: Con base en los restos disponibles, se considera que Razanandrongobe es el miembro de mayor tamaño de los Mesoeucrocodylia terrestres conocidos del Jurásico, y el más grande de todos los Notosuchia en general.

facts.statement: Researchers inferred a total length of 7 meters, a hip height of 1.6 meters, and a weight of 800 to 1000 kilograms based on comparisons with baurusuchids.
facts.quote: Dal Sasso y colaboradores infirieron que tenía una forma corporal similar a la de los baurusúquidos, produciendo una longitud total de 7 metros, una altura a la cadera de 1.6 metros, y un peso de 800 - 1000 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The skull length of Razanandrongobe exceeded that of Barinasuchus, which is estimated at 88 centimeters.
facts.quote: En vida, la longitud de su cráneo sobrepasaba a la de Barinasuchus, la cual ha sido estimada en 88 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe had a highly specialized skull with a robust, rounded U-shaped snout that was taller than it was wide.
facts.quote: Razanandrongobe tenía un cráneo sumamente especializado, con un hocico robusto y redondeado (en forma de U) que era más alto que ancho como en Dakosaurus (de tipo oreinirostral).

facts.statement: Two nearly circular depressions on the palate near the snout front indicate where the first pair of lower teeth would have sat when the mouth was closed.
facts.quote: En el paladar, hay dos depresiones casi circulares situadas cerca del frente del hocico, en donde el primer par de dientes inferiores se habrían situado cuando la boca estaba cerrada.

facts.statement: A slight groove inside the maxilla may have corresponded to a pneumatic opening in the skull also observed in modern alligators.
facts.quote: En el interior del maxilar, había un surco leve, el cual puede haber correspondido a la abertura neumática del cráneo que también es observada en el actual aligátor.

facts.statement: The tip of the jaw lacked teeth in a section of the dentary corresponding to the diameter of more than one tooth.
facts.quote: Curiosamente la punta de la mandíbula carecía de dientes, en una sección del dentario que corresponde al diámetro de más de un diente.

facts.statement: The jaw tip was reinforced by being turned back at an angle of 50 degrees.
facts.quote: La punta de la mandíbula habría estado reforzada al estar dada de vuelta en un ángulo de 50°.

facts.statement: A row of perforations immediately adjacent to the teeth on the inner surface was bounded by a groove toward the back of the jaw.
facts.quote: En la superficie interna había una fila de perforaciones, inmediatamente adyacentes a los dientes, la cual estaba delimitada por un surco hacia la parte posterior de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe had five teeth on each side of the premaxilla, at least ten in each maxilla, and eight in each half of the dentary.
facts.quote: Razanandrongobe tenía cinco dientes a cada lado del premaxilar, al menos diez en cada maxilar maxilar, y ocho en cada mitad del dentario.

facts.statement: All teeth were wider than they were long and nearly vertical.
facts.quote: Todos ellos eran más anchos que largos, y eran casi verticales.

facts.statement: The teeth were thick, did not taper, and were slightly curved (paqudontic).
facts.quote: Estos además eran gruesos, sin estrecharse y están levemente curvados (paquidoncia).

facts.statement: Front teeth were U-shaped or salinon-shaped in cross-section, side teeth were incisiform and nearly oval, and rear teeth were globular.
facts.quote: los dientes del frente de la boca tenían forma de U (o en forma de salinon) en sección transversal, mientras que los de los lados eran incisiformes (en forma de incisivos) y casi ovales en sección transversal, mientras que los dientes más pequeños, situados en la zona posterior tenían una forma globular.

facts.statement: No teeth were particularly hypertrophied like mammalian canines, but the first three dentary teeth were larger than the rest.
facts.quote: Ninguno de los dientes estaba particularmente hipertrofiado a la manera de los dientes caninos de los mamíferos (lo que se conoce como caniniforme), pero los tres primeros dientes del dentario eran más grandes que el resto.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe is the oldest known representative of the Notosuchia group.
facts.quote: La posición filogenética de Razanandrongobe dentro de Notosuchia lo convierte en el más antiguo representante conocido de este grupo.

facts.statement: Razanandrongobe predates all other known Notosuchians by 42 million years, partially filling a ghost lineage.
facts.quote: Razanandrongobe precede a todos estos notosuquios por 42 millones de años, llenando parcialmente este linaje fantasma.

facts.statement: Researchers note that the close relationship between Razanandrongobe and Sebecosuchia must be treated as provisional.
facts.quote: sin embargo, por esta misma razón Dal Sasso y colaboradores señalaron que su cercana relación con los Sebecosuchia — un linaje mucho más reciente, conocido desde el Santoniense en adelante — debe ser tratada como provisional.

facts.statement: Researchers supported the notion that Notosuchians lived mainly on the ancient continent of Gondwana throughout their evolutionary history.
facts.quote: Dal Sasso y colaboradores apoyaron la noción de que los notosuquios vivieron principalmente en el antiguo continente de Gondwana a lo largo de su historia evolutiva

facts.statement: Researchers inferred that Razanandrongobe ate hard objects like bones because its enamel chipped when it bit them, similar to observations in tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: El esmalte se descascarilló a medida que el animal mordía huesos u otros objetos duros, basándose en observaciones similares hechas en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: The skull anatomy supports the inference that Razanandrongobe's diet included hard tissues such as bones and tendons.
facts.quote: La anatomía craneana también apoya que la dieta de Razanandrongobe incluía tejidos duros como huesos y tendones.

facts.statement: The denticles on Razanandrongobe's teeth were adapted to break bones, based on their size, shape, and the presence of a rounded depression at the base between neighboring denticles.
facts.quote: Los dentículos de los dientes de Razanandrongobe estaban adaptados a romper huesos basándose en el parecido de su tamaño, forma y además la presencia de una depresión redondeada en la base entre los dentículos vecinos.

facts.statement: In 2017, Dal Sasso and colleagues suggested that feeding adaptations, combined with its large skull and body size, would have made Razanandrongobe a highly specialized terrestrial predator.
facts.quote: En 2017, Dal Sasso y colaboradores sugirieron que estas adaptaciones para alimentarse, junto con su gran cráneo y tamaño corporal, habrían hecho de Razanandrongobe un depredador terrestre altamente especializado.

facts.quote: Parent group: Baurusuchia

facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
